text:
nate: quick sync 
We need a durable plan for backfilling cost attribution when billing keys are missing from ingest. proposal: nightly backfill job that reconciles traces + metrics to billing records, rather than global auto-prop.

anya: why not realtime best-effort lookup at query time? cheaper storage but slow queries and lots of lookups.

frank: realtime lookup = query latency hit and puts pressure on billing DB. backfill lets us centralize heavy work in batch windows.

paul: backfill concerns: idempotency, partials, ordering. if ingest later receives a key we already inferred, must avoid double-counting.

nate: agree. idea: all inferred attributions should be tagged `attribution_source=inferred_backfill:v1` plus `inference_run_id`. store inference_run_id in a small reconciliation ledger so we can undo or reassign.

billing-ops: also need audit trail per invoice. we can't show "inferred" without explaining methodology on invoices. ops wants confidence thresholds and a rejection path if inference low-confidence.

frank: confidence scoring: use attributes like sample_density, service_stability, tenant_signal_strength. compute a score per inferred mapping; only materialize if score > 0.8. lower scores appear as "estimated" in console but not used for billing unless owner approves.

sre-bot: FYI: large backfill windows spike CPU. recommend rate-limited workers and shard by tenant hash.

anya: storage model: keep a compact attribution record (trace_id -> billing_key | inferred_hash | note). don't duplicate full trace. keep only pointers to original trace id.

paul: GDPR/erasure: if we later need to delete a tenant, inferred mappings must be reversible and deletable. store minimal PII and prefer hashed keys with salt per-environment.

nate: policy: store only irreversible hashes for inferred records and keep mapping provenance. when owner requests delete, we remove ledger entries and re-run backfill to remove counts. document potential gaps.

billing-ops: what about retroactive pricing changes or disputed invoices? need replayable backfill (re-run over historical window) and deterministic results. so algorithm must be deterministic given inputs + salt.

frank: deterministic + salted hashing -> deterministic within env, but if salt changes results shift. we must freeze salt per billing-period and record it in ledger.

anya: performance: run backfill on a rolling 7-day window nightly; keep 90 days of compact attribution records for quick reconciliation; older than 90d aggregate to rollups.

paul: operator controls: UI to mark a service as "exclude-from-inference" (for compliance) and a manual approval flow for inferred attributions to be used for billing.

nate: failure modes: 1) missed join keys -> un-attributed; 2) noisy inference -> wrong bucket. propose alerts when inferred fraction > 10% for a service or inferred confidence-weighted delta > $X/day.

billing-ops: also want a "dispute mode" where a tenant flagged in dispute gets temporary hold and we exclude inferred charges until investigation complete.

frank: implementation tasks: (A) small reconciliation ledger service (immutable append with tombstones) (B) backfill worker that reads traces, computes candidate mappings + scores, writes compact records (C) reconciliation dashboard + revert API.

anya: SDK impact: emit stable join keys when available and `attr_fingerprint_v1` to help backfill. for proxies that strip keys, emit provenance flags so backfill knows to trust/discard.

sre-bot: scheduled: provision backfill-workers cluster canary next Tue.

nate: next steps: frank -> technical design doc + API sketch (due Thu), anya -> SDK header spec PR (Wed), billing-ops -> list required audit fields and approval thresholds (Fri). I'll fold into RFC appendix.

paul: sounds good. small note: include cost estimate for nightly runs (CPU + storage) so finance can OK it.

nate: totally. thanks all, logging this thread for RFC follow-up. :white_check_mark:
